ios.desc:
Like a nutrition label for links.
LegitURL instantly tells you if a link looks trustworthy.

A low score means you probably shouldn’t bother.
Because online, trust should be earned and - NOT assumed.

Whether it’s from a sketchy email, a shortened link, or a suspicious redirect, LegitURL performs a full technical analysis and gives you a clear trust score.
You can also generate a copy-ready report to ask your favorite AI what’s right (or wrong) with the link.

For advanced users, LegitURL analyzes:

• Domain and subdomain structure
• TLS/SSL certificate validation
• HTTP headers and security policies
• JavaScript and cookie behavior
• Redirect chains and tracking patterns
• PDF export of all technical details

Privacy-first by design:

All analysis happens locally on your device.
No cloud. No tracking. No data collection.
And yes… it’s fully open source.

Built for casual users, developers, and privacy nerds alike.

show_hn.title: Show HN: LegitURL: Assess the trustworthiness of unknown links

quotes.text:
We’re in a strange place online where scam and legit links often look identical in their infrastructure and behavior. Fast development cycles, missing headers, lazy security configs,  it’s hard to tell who’s careless and who’s malicious.

Even well-known websites ship with broken HTML, sketchy inline scripts, missing HSTS, or sloppy cookies.

That makes it harder for everyone, tech-savvy or not, to assess whether an unknown link is safe, especially with AI-generated scams on the rise, e.g., trap page —>  auto-redirect stray clicks to legit site.

I built LegitURL to reveal subtle signals that might otherwise go unnoticed.

What it does:

LegitURL (Swift / iOS, open-source):
– Runs offline: parses URL components, flags homograph attacks, entropy spikes, scammy terms
– Sends a single stripped GET request (no cookies, no query) to analyze:
– Silent or shady redirects (even without a Location header)
– TLS cert sanity (CN/SAN match, freshness, sketchy intermediates)
– Missing, broken, or contradictory CSP/HSTS headers
– Cookie flags, expiry, tracking IDs
– HTML structure: stripped comments, <script> tag analysis

All signals are shown transparently. You can export a PDF for humans or a JSON report for LLMs.

It’s not a malware detector or blacklist checker,  it’s a structural/behavioral analyzer.

Fully on-device. Most links resolve in under 2s depending on latency.
